I will check each chapter of the draft against the gate test, looking only for structural damage, not mere compression.

---

**Ch 011 draft — the "banshee scream / sheet trap" scene**

In the source, the narrator's escape plan is explicit: she grabs a sheet, positions herself by the door, shrieks about a badger, and when the door opens she throws the sheet over the old woman, pushes the tangled group down, and steps over them into the hall. The draft compresses all of this away. Instead the draft has her say she cannot get out the main door, then says "The side door swung inward on a quiet hinge" and she simply walks through it into the lord's room — with no hall escape, no guard encounter, no chaos in the corridor.

Yet immediately after she enters the lord's room, the draft has: *"Somewhere behind me, in the hall I had just left, feet gathered. Keys, orders, the busy clatter of a household who had lost track of its troublesome charge."* This implies she was already in the hall and retreated into the lord's room because pursuers were coming — consistent with the source's hallway-escape sequence. But the draft never showed her in the hall; she went directly from her room through the side door. The phrase "the hall I had just left" has no referent in the preceding draft text — she never entered or left a hall in the draft.

Then in the dialogue under the bed, the old woman says: *"Only a moment ago,"* as the complete answer to "How and when?" — the source continues *"and she—well, she threw a blanket over my husband and me."* The draft cuts the husband detail. This matters structurally because later in the source the lord says "us" as the dreaded plural — meaning him and the maiden. But in the draft, the "us" line is preserved (*"You may leave us." / "Us. My heart stopped at that terrible plural."*), and the "husband and me" cut only removes colour, not a referent needed for "us." So that is not a finding.

The real finding is "the hall I had just left":
